rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so this experiment tests the baseline performance of a simple RNA-only model with PCA encoding. It clarifies whether basic RNA features alone can achieve reasonable accuracy, establishing a reference point before exploring more complex multimodal configurations.

Existing evidence shows config_001 (RNA-only, singleprofile) achieves 0.4849 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile setting while keeping RNA encoder and image encoder consistent. It addresses uncertainty about whether multiprofile improves performance, a key design choice, without changing multiple parameters simultaneously.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile (config_002, 0.5907 accuracy) outperforms singleprofile (config_001, 0.4849). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool (config_002) with transformer aggregation in multiprofile improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It balances exploitation of multiprofile's benefit with exploration of aggregation choices, which are critical for model design.

Existing evidence shows that for RNA-only models, multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (config_002, 0.59 accuracy) outperforms singleprofile. This experiment tests replacing pca_n2000 with scvi_n200 RNA encoder in the same multiprofile/avgpool setup to isolate the impact of RNA encoder choice. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether scvi_n200 (a more complex encoder) improves performance compared to pca_n2000, while maintaining other parameters consistent with the currently strongest RNA-only configuration.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with multiprofile and avgpool aggregation (config_005) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.6501). This experiment tests adding image data (resnet50) to this strong RNA-only baseline, isolating the effect of multimodal fusion. It balances exploitation of the promising RNA encoder and profile setting with exploration of multimodal benefits, avoiding unnecessary changes to other parameters.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and multiprofile setting (config_005) achieve the highest accuracy (0.6501). The next experiment should test whether adding image data (multimodal) with the same RNA encoder and aggregation method (avgpool) can improve performance. Config_036 isolates the effect of image data by using the same RNA encoder and aggregation as config_005 but introduces a more advanced image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) and concat fusion, which could reveal if multimodal approaches can surpass unimodal performance.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and concat fusion achieves high accuracy (0.7150). This experiment tests whether switching to resnet50 image encoder and weighted fusion (while keeping scvi_n200 and avgpool) improves performance, isolating the impact of image encoder and fusion method. It balances exploration of critical design choices without overcomplicating the setup.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l image encoder with concat fusion and avgpool aggregation (config_036) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation (while keeping other parameters identical) improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It balances exploitation of the strong image encoder and exploration of a key design choice.

Existing evidence shows that using 'imagenet_vit_l' as the image encoder and 'transformer' aggregation significantly improves performance (config_038: 0.7207 accuracy). This experiment tests whether switching from 'concat' to 'weighted' fusion (a critical design choice) further enhances performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It builds on the strong prior evidence for ViT and transformer aggregation while exploring a key component of multimodal integration.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (e.g., config_039) achieve high validation accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether switching to scgpt RNA encoder (while keeping image encoder, aggregation, and fusion methods identical) improves performance, isolating the impact of RNA representation. It directly compares a promising RNA encoder (scvi_n200) with a newer one (scgpt) in the same multimodal setup, addressing uncertainty about RNA encoder effectiveness without changing multiple factors.
